questions.q: On a Q-sphere plot, what do blob size and blob color represent?
options: Size = qubit index, color = gate type
Size = probability of that basis state, color = relative phase of that basis state's amplitude
Size = number of shots, color = measurement error
Size and color both represent the same thing: shot count
questions.explain: Each basis state with nonzero probability appears as a blob whose size encodes its probability and whose color encodes its relative phase.

questions.q: For the 2-qubit Bell state (amplitudes 0.7071068 on 00 and 11, exactly 0 on 01/10), what does plot_state_qsphere actually render?
options: Four equal-size blobs at 00, 01, 10, and 11
Two equal-size, equal-color blobs at 00 and 11, with nothing at 01 or 10
One large blob at 00 only
Four blobs of varying sizes
questions.explain: Only 00 and 11 have nonzero amplitude (0.7071068 each, giving equal 0.5 probability), so only those two equal-size, same-color blobs appear. 01 and 10 have zero amplitude and produce no blob at all.

questions.q: For the 3-qubit GHZ state (amplitudes 0.7071068 on 000 and 111, zero elsewhere), how many blobs appear on the Q-sphere and where?
options: Eight blobs, one at each possible 3-bit string
Two equal-size, equal-color blobs at 000 and 111, with nothing at the other six positions
Three blobs, one per qubit
One blob covering the whole sphere
questions.explain: Just like the Bell state scaled to 2 qubits, the GHZ state populates exactly two of its eight possible basis-state positions (000 and 111) with equal probability and equal phase; the other six positions have zero amplitude and show nothing.

questions.q: What does plot_state_city show that plot_bloch_multivector cannot, for an entangled multi-qubit state?
options: Nothing — they show identical information
The real and imaginary amplitude components across all basis states, which captures the entanglement structure a per-qubit Bloch arrow can't represent
The number of shots used in the experiment
The specific hardware backend used
questions.explain: state-city draws 3D bars for the real and imaginary amplitude of every basis state, directly showing entanglement and relative phase structure. A Bloch sphere only has meaning for a single qubit's own state and cannot represent this for an entangled system.

questions.q: Why is it fundamentally wrong to try to draw a separate Bloch sphere for each qubit in the Bell state and expect it to fully describe the system?
options: It's not wrong — Bloch spheres work perfectly fine for entangled qubits
Because an entangled multi-qubit state has no single-qubit Bloch vector that fully describes it; the correlation between qubits isn't captured by either qubit's individual state alone
Because Bloch spheres only work for 3 or more qubits
Because plot_bloch_multivector doesn't exist in Qiskit
questions.explain: Entanglement is a property of the joint system, not of either qubit individually. Each qubit's own reduced state in an entangled pair doesn't carry the correlation information, so no per-qubit Bloch vector captures what the Q-sphere shows directly across basis states.
